title: GOV-0147: an unresolved merge conflict from #276 is committed into GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md — gate, suite and diff-filter=U are all blind to it
problem:
> ⚠️ **BODY CORRECTED 2026-09-04 — see the "provenance corrected" comment below.** The
> original body asserted that the two halves were *"consecutive rungs C and D of the
> badf-uat ladder."* **That is false.** At `595b032` rung D did not exist; the two sides
> were two different work packages' ledger sections. Rung D was appended INTO the stale
> block a day later by `272e603`. The resolution (keep everything) is unchanged; the reason
> is. An independent review caught it before the fix landed.

🏛 **SARCHI** — `main@310a660`. An unresolved git merge conflict is committed into the doctrine, and nothing in the repo can see it.

## The defect

`docs/governance/GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md` carries all three conflict markers as **live prose**:

```
2086:<<<<<<< HEAD
2136:=======
2209:>>>>>>> 1150843 (feat(gate): the enforcement-input ratchet -- expected_surfaces mandatory
                      from WP-2026-0126, coverage counted, unmatchable refused, may-touch unified)
```

**Provenance:** `git log -S '<<<<<<< HEAD'` returns exactly one commit — **`595b032`, "BADF-WP-0126: the enforcement-input ratchet … (#276)"**. The `>>>>>>>` label names that same work package, so the conflict was produced and committed by that PR.

**It is not fenced.** Counting fence lines before 2090 gives **2 — even, therefore outside any code block.** These are bare document lines, rendered as content.

## Why it is not cosmetic: the block is an accumulation nobody ever chose between

```
2086  <<<<<<< HEAD
2087  ## badf-uat → deterministic G10 controls …        rung C   (#273 / GOV-0120)
2136  =======
2137  ## badf-uat → SHADOWED — representative calibration …   rung D   (#277 / GOV-0124)
2209  >>>>>>> 1150843 (…)
```

**Measured provenance — a committed conflict block is not frozen, later commits append into it:**

```text
commit    rung C   rung D   markers
bc7ca27      1        0        0
595b032      1        0        1     <- markers committed here; rung D DID NOT EXIST
272e603      1        1        1     <- rung D appended INTO the stale block, next day
310a660      1        1        1
```

At `595b032` the two sides were **two different work packages' ledger sections** — WP-0125's `badf-uat` rung C against WP-0126's enforcement-input ratchet. `272e603` (BADF-WP-0131, #296) later inserted rung D immediately after the `=======`, which is why the "theirs" side now holds two unrelated sections. **The correct resolution is *keep everything, delete the marker lines*** — not because the halves are alternatives, but because by now they are an accumulation nobody ever chose between. That is exactly the case a hurried `--theirs`/`--ours` destroys.

A secondary rendering defect rides along: line 2139 is non-blank and immediately precedes `=======`, so GitHub renders it as a setext `<h1>`.

## Nothing detects it, and that is the governance finding

- `badf_gate.py repo` → **PASS**
- the full suite → **1217 tests, 0 failures**
- `git diff --diff-filter=U` → **empty**, because it is committed content, not an unmerged index entry

**Every instrument this repo has for merge damage looks at the index or at bytes-vs-lockfile. A conflict that has been committed is, to all of them, ordinary text.** The one check that would catch it — "no governed doc contains a conflict marker at a non-fenced line" — does not exist.

## It gets worse under composition, which is how it surfaced

**Open PR #316 appends badf-uat rung E to the *incoming* half.** After that merge, three of the ladder's five rungs live inside the conflict block. **This is not a reason to hold #316** — the damage predates it and #316's own content is correct — but the region gets harder to repair with each landing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The three marker lines at 2086 / 2136 / 2209 are removed and **all content on both sides retained** — the block accumulated across three commits and no half is an alternative to the other, so a resolution that drops either loses shipped doctrine. Verify afterwards that each affected section appears exactly once and that the badf-uat headings read A→B→C→D in document order.
2. Line 2139's setext-`<h1>` artifact is resolved (blank line inserted or the line re-flowed).
3. **A guard that fails on this class:** a test asserting no file under `docs/governance/` contains `^<<<<<<< `, `^=======$` or `^>>>>>>> ` **at a non-fenced line**. It MUST be fence-aware — a naive matcher will fire on legitimate documentation quoting a marker inside a code block, and this repo does contain such prose elsewhere.
4. **The guard must be shown to fail and then pass:** run it against `310a660` (expect RED, naming this file and these lines) and against the fixed tree (expect GREEN). A guard never observed failing is not admitted (`docs/learnings/a-guard-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-guard.md`).
5. **Adversarial clause:** sweep **every** tracked text file, not just `docs/governance/`, for committed markers at non-fenced lines, and report the full result. **If the sweep finds only this instance, state the matcher and the fence-detection method** so a reader can judge whether zero elsewhere is a finding or a limitation. Any further instance is filed separately, not fixed here.
6. **Declared non-coverage:** this does not attempt to detect *semantically* mis-resolved merges — a conflict resolved by silently dropping a half leaves no marker and is out of reach of any textual guard. Say so rather than implying the guard closes that class.

## Provenance and a correction I owe

Found by a BADF verification seat during the 4-way composition review of #316/#324/#326/#328. **I had briefed two seats that this marker was benign documentation about merge conflicts** — a false control I asserted without measuring. The seat disproved it three ways (fence-state walk, both halves carrying real `##` headings, `git log -S` provenance) rather than accepting the briefing. **The instruction I gave alongside it — detect conflicts with `git diff --diff-filter=U` — is correct and unaffected; the justification was wrong, and it would have led a reader to dismiss the real thing.**

**Tier: patch** — document repair plus a test. **Lean mode: advisory.**
